extracted.intended_audience: Contracting Officers, acquisition/procurement personnel (DoD/Navy) and field contracting offices implementing OMB Circular A-76
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for Contracting Officers implementing OMB Circular A-76 for Commercial Industrial Type Activities (CITA), covering cost estimates, cost comparisons, solicitation methods, disclosure/reveal rules, review/verification periods, appeals vs protests, and organizational/training recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealed in-house cost estimate submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A sealed in-house cost estimate must be submitted to the Contracting Officer by the required submission date for bids and proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The researcher found no written guidance on actions if the estimate is submitted late; contracting officers indicated they monitor this closely and may direct negotiators to maintain close interface with the task group and immediately extend the bid opening date if a late submission appears possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government in-house cost estimate required for cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost comparison cannot be accomplished without the Government in-house cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing and proposed directives require use of firm bid/offer procedure and the cost comparison if in-house performance is to be based on lower cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for late submission of the Government cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no definitive clause guidance for how to proceed if the Government cost estimate is submitted late; possibilities discussed include automatic extension of the solicitation or rejection under late-proposal provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many interviewees considered automatic extension unacceptable because it would favor the Government; contracting personnel reported practice of extending bid opening proactively to avoid late submission issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Government in-house estimate as a proposal subject to late-proposal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost comparison clause used in many negotiated solicitations indicates the Government in-house cost estimate will be considered a proposal and thus subject to the 'Late Proposals, Modification of Proposals, and Withdrawal of Proposals' provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the late-proposal provision applies, late government estimates would 'not be considered' and thus appear to have to be rejected even though a cost comparison is required — this creates a conflict between directives and some contracting clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to reveal Government in-house cost estimate (formal advertising)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Formally Advertised Procurements (including Small Business Restricted Advertising) the Government cost estimate will be revealed at the bid opening (or as soon as practicable thereafter) to contractors who submit a bid and to the labor union of Government employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since formal advertising methods satisfy the cost comparison requirements, this timing is satisfactory under those methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to reveal Government in-house cost estimate (negotiated solicitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: For negotiated solicitations the clause stipulates that at the conclusion of negotiations the Contracting Officer will set a time and place for public opening of the Government in-house estimate, provide notification, open and record the in-house cost estimate, and provide copies to interested personnel upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observers indicated this procedure was not being followed for 8(a) set-asides and that the negotiated clause coverage is deficient with regard to special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reveal in-house estimate in 8(a) negotiated procurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers indicated the existing clause for negotiated procurements needed modification to indicate that the Government in-house cost estimate will not be revealed in the case of 8(a) negotiated procurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendance by union representatives and interested contracting personnel at the opening in 8(a) cases was considered inappropriate because it could give the 8(a) offeror an unfair advantage (e.g., by enabling later lower bids during resolicitation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance restrictions at in-house estimate opening (8(a) cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendance of union representatives and interested contracting personnel at the opening of the in-house estimate in 8(a) cases may not be appropriate; even the attendance of only the 8(a) offeror could compromise process integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No instances were located where cost comparison clauses had been modified for 8(a) special use; concerns center on fairness and potential for advantaging an offeror.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement of preliminary cost comparison results at bid opening
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding at bid openings includes assuring procedures are followed to avoid accusations of unfair comparison and making a statement indicating the preliminary results of the initial cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required statements must specify that preliminary calculations indicate either in-house or contract operation is most economical but final determination will await verification of calculations and completion of responsibility determinations in the case of a low contractor offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two review periods and public announcement procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two review periods: the first at bid/public opening (initial cost comparison) and the second after Task Group Decision Summary Recommendation approval, when the Contracting Officer announces results and withholds award pending public review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both clauses in use indicate award will be withheld a minimum of five workdays; the Cost Comparison Handbook indicates 5 to 15 working days; NAVSUP questioned whether five days is sufficient because mail notification may consume the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public review period length and notification considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum public review is typically five working days; handbook allows up to fifteen working days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experienced personnel preferred fifteen days because mail notification can consume much of a five-day period and deny bidders an opportunity to examine the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification/audit of the Government cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Two times when discrepancies may be uncovered: during audit of the cost comparison form by an independent auditing activity, and during the public review of the cost comparison and Decision Summary Recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If minor discrepancies are noted, the audit certificate is executed; significant discrepancies are reported to the Task Group Chairperson with impact and recommendations on correction and resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'significant discrepancy' in the in-house estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no definitive written guidance on what constitutes a 'significant discrepancy'; interviewees generally defined it as one that altered the relative standing between the low bidder and the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operational definition should guide auditors and contracting personnel in reporting and recommending corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions when Government estimate cannot be corrected timely
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Government cost estimate cannot be corrected in a timely manner (by the bids/proposals expiration), some negotiators thought the solicitation would have to be cancelled and resolicited, though requirements differ for new starts vs conversions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a new start the Government estimate will be rejected and a contract awarded; for a conversion the solicitation may be cancelled. The researcher found no requirement that the solicitation must be cancelled in all cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals vs protests under OMB Circular A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular historically has been silent about conferring substantive rights enforceable in GAO protests; GAO holds A-76 directives are Executive policy matters beyond GAO jurisdiction. The 1979 Circular states it does not create substantive/procedural basis for challenge except as regards the internal appeals process in Section 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11's appeals process resolves determinations between in-house and contract performance internally; it does not authorize external action or judicial review, and appeals are reviewed by an official at the same level or higher than the original Approving Authority; agency decisions are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer responsibility to determine commercial source availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Circular guidelines, the Contracting Officer has new responsibilities in determining the availability of commercial sources to perform a specific CITA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early participation by contracting personnel in the assessment phase of the CITA cycle is recommended; development of sources of supply has traditionally centered on contracting expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying solely on informational solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Informational solicitations by themselves are not satisfactory for deciding to retain a function in-house due to non-availability of commercial sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use informational solicitations only in conjunction with other required methods; if no commercial interest is expressed, CBD notices are still required before deciding to retain performance in-house.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBD notices need clearer guidance on sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce Business Daily (CBD) notices are of questionable value and the Office of Federal Procurement Policy should provide more definitive guidance on the use of CBD notices including what constitutes a sufficient response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the interim, Contracting Officers should be hesitant to use CBD notices in lieu of a formal solicitation to avoid unnecessarily extending the acquisition process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote multifunctional solicitations and combined requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers should take a more active role in developing multifunctional solicitations and consider combining the same requirement at different organizations into a single solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages include lower acquisition and contract administration costs; Contracting Officers must judge desirability given potential impacts on small/disadvantaged business participation and coordinate early with supported organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control communications to prevent premature release of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting personnel must be fully familiar with directives relating to communications with interested groups to prevent premature release of information that could embarrass the command or attack system integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is important given the sensitive nature of CITA contracting and likely inquiries from unions, Congress, industry, and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review organizational/staffing structure and consider dedicated branches
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers should review their organization and staffing, consider establishing dedicated Service Branches or a separate Contract Administration Branch to process CITA requests effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps assure effective and efficient processing as program workload grows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor field implementation and adjust resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Naval Supply Systems Command should monitor field activity implementation and provide additional resources commensurate with program growth to avoid worsening workload problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field contracting offices should ensure existing resources are optimally organized to support projected program growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject inadequate statements of work and enforce milestone integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers should reject statements of work not adequate for solicitation purposes and require resubmission rather than attempting corrections after receipt; internal milestones should be established and maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract negotiators must become familiar with elements of a good CITA work statement and actively manage milestones; Naval Supply Systems Command should set realistic Procurement Administrative Lead Time standards for CITA contracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitize procurement responsibility agreements between commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Naval Supply Systems Command and Naval Facilities Engineering Command should definitize agreements about which command will procure a specific service function to develop specialized expertise and enhance coordination, preparation, and submission of statements of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear responsibilities assist contracting offices in specialization and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish dedicated training programs on key reference material
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting offices should establish dedicated training programs centered around key reference materials to prepare personnel for CITA contracting and cost comparison processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training will help negotiators answer questions at pre-bid/proposal conferences and perform professional bid/public opening duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support Task Group internal planning and early coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting offices should support internal planning of the Task Group to ensure realistic milestones, accurate and complete statements of work, and maintenance of system integrity by coordinating schedules early in the planning cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is best accomplished before receipt of the purchase request in the contracting office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise DoD/Navy directives to align with policy guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Defense and Navy directives should be revised and clarified to conform with existing A-76 policy guidelines to enhance consistent policy implementation by field contracting offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This would improve ability to achieve consistent implementation and reduce confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add separate DAR coverage for service contracting including CITA
rubrics_metrics.description: Defense Acquisition Regulation should include separate coverage of service contracting with a distinct section on CITA Support Service Contracting addressing inconsistencies and voids (8(a) set-asides, options, cost comparison, late submission treatment, 'significant discrepancy', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation of the Firm Bid/Offer procedure (DAR Case 76-144) into the regulatory framework is suggested as a step toward this objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain integrity and avoid compromising actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting professionals should take aggressive action to assure the integrity of the system is beyond reproach and assess their actions to avoid inadvertently placing themselves in compromising positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procurement personnel should provide guidance to the Task Group Chairperson on Standards of Conduct and ensure all members understand duties and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer formal advertising and performance-oriented statements of work
rubrics_metrics.description: In most instances, formal advertising methods should be used to accomplish the Cost Comparison for potential conversions and should require a performance-oriented statement of work detailing what is to be accomplished but not how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal advertising combined with performance-oriented SOWs supports equitable competition and effective cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximize use of pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting offices should make maximum use of pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences and site visits because many contractors are not aware of CITA concepts and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires negotiators to be familiar with the cost comparison process to provide intelligent answers at conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat Government as another potential source of supply (equity)
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve equitability and integrity, Contracting Officers should consider the Government simply another potential source of supply and apply the same procedures regarding submission of the in-house cost estimate, negotiations, distribution of solicitation amendments, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the Task Group Chairperson equivalent to a private firm's manager and direct communications accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish additional Government costs as award factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional costs to the Government of contracting-out are award factors (not evaluation factors) and should be emphasized at pre-bid/proposal conferences and by other methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction permits clear separation between contractors' quoted price and the total cost to the Government if a contract is awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure personnel involved in bid/public opening review CITA directives
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract negotiators and personnel who will be directly involved in a Bid or Public Opening for contracting-out actions should review existing CITA directives to ensure professional accomplishment of the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarity with directives helps assure correct bid opening procedures and avoids misunderstandings that could attack system integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officers review Circular appeals guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers should review the guidance in the Circular to ensure a firm understanding of the appeals concept, its limits, and the Contracting Officer's role relative to appeals and protests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding appeals is significant for placing the Contracting Officer's role in proper perspective during determinations between in-house and contract performance.
